newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index rallies, seen higher on arb.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index rallies, seen higher on arb.

text.p: Singapore shares rallied sharply on Friday morning, spurred by rumours the government might abolish a system of dual listings for strategic companies.

By the 0430 GMT lunchtime break, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index was 2.29 percent or 43.39 points higher at 1,935.16. Total market volume was a healthy 149 million shares with 197 shares higher and 113 lower.
Dealers said much of the volume was by locals selling the foreign tranches of blue chip companies such as Singapore Press and SIA and buying back their local shares.

"They are playing the arb(itrage)," said one institutional dealer with a major European bank. "By any standards the local shares are too cheap...People have finally woken up to that and I think they will go higher still."
Several top Singapore companies, including all four of the big banks DBS, OCBC, OUB and UOB, have split listings on strategic grounds.
The local tranches can only be bought by Singaporeans or Singapore companies. Foreign tranches can be bought by anyone.
The local tranches of SIA and SPH are both included in the 30-share STI and were largely responsible for the early surge in the index on Friday, dealers said.
The government-owned Singapore Technologies group has scrapped the dual listings of its five units in the last week, leading to speculation that other companies may follow suit.
Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.
SIA's local shares were last up 35 cents at Singapore $8.35, while its foreign tranche was down 30 cents at S$11.30.
Singapore Press's local tranche stood at S$14.30, up S$0.90, with its foreign shares at S$24.50, down 20 cents.

Elsewhere on the market, shares in hotel group Amara Holdings jumped 80 percent to a high of S$0.54 on their first day of trading. The public portion of its initial public offer (IPO) was 39.6 times subscribed at S$0.30 each.
By lunchtime, almost 65 million Amara shares had traded and the share had settled at S$0.49.
